name: physx-release-flags
title: physx-linux workflow: create dependency releases as prereleases, never as the repo's latest release
issue: The user said (2026-10-13): make sure the releases are appropriately tagged because they are not engine releases. The repo convention is that every release is a prerelease (Box-Demo, physx-dependencies, and now physx-dependencies-linux-5.6.1 after the orchestrator edited it). In .github/workflows/physx-linux.yml the publish job creates the release with `gh release create ... --title ... --notes ...` (~l.249-252): add `--prerelease --latest=false`, change the title to `PhysX ${PHYSX_VERSION} for Linux (build dependency, not an engine release)`, and the notes to: `Build dependency, not an N2Engine release.` followed by one sentence that these are prebuilt static Release libraries of NVIDIA PhysX built by the PhysX Linux workflow and downloaded by the engine CMake with a pinned SHA256 (cmake/PhysXLinuxHashes.cmake), and that the archives carry the PhysX LICENSE.md. Also add the same wording as a comment above the step so the intent survives. Nothing else changes: no trigger, permission, action version or build step changes. Do NOT publish or dispatch anything. Verify by reading the file that the YAML still parses (python -c yaml via a quick check or careful inspection) and that the dry-run (pull_request path trigger) still runs and passes on CI.
acceptance: The PhysX Linux dry run still passes
The release-creation command uses --prerelease --latest=false and the dependency wording
notes: Tiny. The already-published release was fixed by hand (prerelease, not latest, renamed, new body).
